name: Western Customs House
region_detail: At the western outlet of Lake Ophar into Cador proper, away from the town of Westbridge. The Westbridge record prefix denotes administrative affiliation, not territorial sovereignty.
site_type: customs house | Inhabited locations | Operating royal customs installation and river inspection station.
history: Following the Edict of the East in 3E-991, Marquis Cedric Bellamy secured a royal concession authorizing his administration to maintain a customs house where Lake Ophar drains into the great westward-flowing river of Cador. This permits the collection of authorized duties from commercial shipping that may never enter Westbridge itself. The concession is a delegated royal privilege rather than an extension of the marquisate’s territorial boundaries.
current_state: In 3E-992 the customs house is operating under Bellamy’s administration. Officials inspect commercial cargoes, collect authorized duties on goods entering and leaving Cador, and record vessel movements. Independent merchants object to inspections and costs; smugglers seek alternative landings and overland routes. Bellamy’s separate proposed fortified station at the mouth of the Storbruhn is not this installation and is the subject of the War of the Waters.
inhabitants: Customs clerks and inspectors, guards acting under Bellamy’s authority, visiting river crews and merchants. No named resident commander or permanent staffing complement has been established.
danger_level: Low ordinarily for lawful travelers; potential for confrontation during inspections or disputes. River conditions and any organized criminal activity may present additional hazards.
points_of_interest:
Customs office and cargo records; inspection landing and facilities; duty collection point; access to the lake outlet and the river into Cador. Precise layout and extent of fortifications are undetermined.

Unresolved elements: Exact hex and precise location on the outlet; formal name if adopted; specific terms and tariffs of the concession; staffing, physical layout, and defenses; arrangements with the neighboring Cadorian authorities.
discovery: At the western outlet of Lake Ophar into Cador proper, away from the town of Westbridge. The Westbridge record prefix denotes administrative affiliation, not territorial sovereignty.
